title: ‘The Frosty Caucasus’
subtitle: An Account of a Walk through Part of the Range and of an Ascent of Elbruz in the Summer of 1874
summary: An English mountaineer’s account of a climbing journey in the western Caucasus in the summer of 1874, with A. W. Moore, H. Walker, and F. Gardiner, the Swiss guide Peter Knubel, and a Mingrelian dragoman, Paul. They sail from Odessa along the Crimean and Circassian coasts, go by Poti and Kutais to Tiflis and back, and then walk up the Rion and over the main chain to the valleys of the Tcherek, Bezingi, Tchegem, and the Baksan, staying with local chiefs. From Urusbieh they climb Elbruz. They return by the green country north of the mountain, Utchkulan, and the Nakhar Pass, and come down the Klütch and Kodor valleys to Soukhoum Kaleh on the Black Sea. The tone is dry and often ironic, about guides, hosts, and prices. The book has six wood engravings by Edward Whymper from Walker’s photographs and a folding map.
omitted_from_reading: The half-title and the printer’s imprint on its back, the printed contents, the list of illustrations, the book’s title printed above Chapter I, and the publisher’s advertisement are in the JSON only.
notes_on_text: The plates are wood engravings by Edward Whymper from photographs taken during the journey by Horace Walker. The folding map is shown at the end of the book; at the width of a page its names cannot be read, and the scan at the Internet Archive shows it in full.
